# Every `smethods["open"]` door that is NOT socketOpenWithBlock and NOT
# unsupported(…), with what it does about its block.
#
# ⛔ THIS FILE DOES NOT DEFINE THE POPULATION. TestEveryOpenDoorIsAccountedFor
# derives that by parsing the package, on every platform, and compares the two
# both ways: a door missing from here fails, and a row here for a door that no
# longer exists fails too. That is the whole point — #931 wrote the socket doors
# out in prose and the prose had already lost UNIXServer, and #939 found a fourth
# door (Resolv::DNS) that no list held at all. A list cannot be the authority on
# its own subject.
#
# ⛔ The ALIAS form (`x.smethods["open"] = y.smethods["new"]`) can never appear
# here: the test refuses it outright, because the aliased method has no block
# parameter and so no configuration of it can honour one.
#
# Format: <file>:<receiver> <reason>
# The reason must say what happens to the block, and must name what PROVES it —
# or say plainly that nothing does, so an unverified door is countable rather
# than quiet.

# ───────── honours its block: yields, closes on the way out, answers the block's value
io.go:cFile File.open yields and closes through the RUBY-level #close (io.go:598, via ioYieldAndClose), so a subclass override runs; covered behaviourally by the core/file and core/io spec files and by TestEveryWayToGetAWritableFileFlushesAtShutdown's block-free forms.
io_class.go:cIO IO.open yields via ioYieldAndClose (io_class.go:43) after forFd builds the stream; same close path as File.open.
io.go:cls StringIO.open yields, then closes AND drops the backing string (#string => nil) in a defer, even on a raise (io.go:2349).
dir.go:cDir Dir.open yields and marks the handle closed in a defer, even on a raise (dir.go:348).
net_ftp.go:ftp Net::FTP.open yields the connected client through ftpWithClose, which closes on unwind (net_ftp.go:110).
sqlite3.go:cls SQLite3::Database.open yields and closes the database in a defer (sqlite3.go:102); SQLite3::Database.new shares the same func.
bolt.go:cls The bbolt database's open yields and closes the handle (bolt.go:76), returning the block's value.

# ───────── does NOT honour its block. #950
# Takes `_ *Proc` and discards it. Listed here rather than fixed so the count is
# visible: one door, on a binding surface, not in MRI core.
#
# ⛔ augeas.go:cls WAS THE OTHER ONE, and its row said the fix was "blocked"
# because rbgo's Augeas had no #close for socketOpenWithBlock to call and
# go-ruby-augeas's handle exposes no Close. That was the WRONG LAYER: #close in
# the gem frees a C handle, but what it makes OBSERVABLE is `nil` plus a poisoned
# object that raises SystemCallError from every method after it — a flag and a
# guard, needing nothing from the dependency. The door now goes through
# socketOpenWithBlock, so it is correct by construction and owes this file no
# row at all.
images.go:cls UNSPECIFIED, not a known defect. Images::Image.open discards its block (images.go:93). go-ruby-images' README documents no Ruby `Image.open` and no block form at all — it documents the Go library (`images.Open("photo.jpg")`) — and ruby-vips and MiniMagick spell this operation without a block, so "no block form" may be the contract to DOCUMENT rather than a gap to fill. See #950.
